notes: All public exact shapes still run two GPU launches inside owned-workspace wrappers: A-pack then exact compute.
Public exact paths already bypass old generic B repack/unshuffle helper launches and consume raw b_q plus raw shuffled b_scale_sh.
Top-level contract still includes b_shuffle, but exact fast paths ignore it.

dead_or_exhausted_lanes: exact_public_graph_replay_r1 is dead on runner: empty HIP graphs and catastrophic benchmark regression
host-only wrapper collapse lanes such as nocheck / cpp-return were noise-to-worse
m4 one-shot producer-consumer ready-flag design is dead
m32 single-CTA serial single-launch sweep is dead and catastrophic
pure kernel-body-only tuning cannot plausibly bridge 13.406us to <=7us

open_non_apack_lanes.deleted_cost_center: raw row-major B feed with worst inter-lane stride plus per-step shuffled-scale decode on exact m16
open_non_apack_lanes.why_large: m16 has the weakest latency hiding, the largest B stride, and the largest wall-vs-self gap among thin shapes
open_non_apack_lanes.major_risk: caller-provided b_shuffle contract may not map to a directly consumable exact-kernel feed layout
open_non_apack_lanes.fast_falsifier: if the replacement still needs a per-call B pack kernel, kill the branch unless that layout is already supplied by the caller

open_non_apack_lanes.deleted_cost_center: 8x raw-B reread across y-tiles plus repeated scale decode
open_non_apack_lanes.why_large: grid.y=8 gives real B reuse economics on the live exact m256 path
open_non_apack_lanes.major_risk: one-shot B prep can overpay if not truly amortized by reuse
open_non_apack_lanes.fast_falsifier: if measured B-prep traffic is not amortized by the reread reduction, kill it

open_non_apack_lanes.why_large: still a real reuse bucket, but weaker than m256
open_non_apack_lanes.major_risk: pack/setup cost can exceed the two-pass reread saving
open_non_apack_lanes.fast_falsifier: if pack/setup traffic exceeds removed reread traffic, kill it

open_non_apack_lanes.deleted_cost_center: scalar byte copies and unnecessary register clearing in thin exact kernels
open_non_apack_lanes.why_large: m32/m64/m256 already use a better vector-load pattern that m4/m16 still lack
open_non_apack_lanes.fast_falsifier: no measurable reduction in vector loads or register pressure

open_non_apack_lanes.deleted_cost_center: repeated VGPR-mediated B ingress after a B-direct win exists
open_non_apack_lanes.why_large: only becomes credible after a usable wide-shape B contract is in place
open_non_apack_lanes.major_risk: LDS staging without real reuse just adds traffic and pressure
open_non_apack_lanes.fast_falsifier: no measured reduction in B reread or live-range pressure

critical_contract_findings: Do not assume b_scale_sh is row-major [n,16]; benchmark-mode live layout is opaque.
The in-repo helper _get_b_preshuffled_mfma_fp4(b_q) returns shape [n/16, k_half*16], so it is not a drop-in stand-in for the currently visible top-level b_shuffle contract.
Any b_shuffle-based lane must verify the actual runner contract before remote spend.
bottom_line: Stop spending on helper A-pack micro-variants. The best no-A-pack research direction is B-feed law and wide-shape B reuse, led by exact m16 for thin-shape B bandwidth/coalescing and exact m256 for B reuse economics. Pure kernel-body tuning is too small to reach <=7us from the current 13.406us anchor.
